name: scryer-prolog
desc: Modern ISO Prolog implementation written mostly in Rust
why: A modern ISO Prolog in Rust opens a logic programming world most developers never touch.

brief.what_it_is: Scryer Prolog is a free ISO Prolog system written mostly in Rust. You give it Prolog source files, which it consults (loads), or type queries at its interactive toplevel, and it prints answers or bindings such as X = "Scryer Prolog!". It includes a WAM-based engine and a large library set, covering constraint solving (clp(B), clp(Z)), DCGs, tabling, TCP sockets, an HTTP server and client, and cryptography. It can also be built as a WebAssembly package or used as a library from other programs.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the goal is to become to ISO Prolog what GHC is to Haskell: an open source, industrial-strength production environment that is also a testbed for bleeding-edge research in logic and constraint programming, itself written in a high-level language.
brief.how_it_works: It is an implementation of the Warren Abstract Machine (WAM) in Rust, built in phases following Warren's Abstract Machine tutorial. Its best-known internal trick is a packed UTF-8 representation of strings and partial strings, which the README says cuts memory use by up to 24-fold compared with one WAM cell per character. Tabling is implemented on top of delimited continuations (reset/3, shift/1) rather than as a separate engine mode.

commands_seen.context: Clone the source repository for a native build from a local checkout.
Compile the optimised executable, which lands in target/release/scryer-prolog.
Install the binary from the git repository into $HOME/.cargo/bin.
Install the latest crates.io release; the README warns this can lag behind git.
Start Scryer Prolog from the Docker Hub image with one command.
Run Scryer Prolog and consult program.pl, passing the file on the command line.
Consult a file from inside the toplevel.
Load a bundled library module before using its predicates.
Shows that double-quoted text is a character list by default (double_quotes flag is chars).

brief.install_notes: Precompiled binaries are on the GitHub releases page for several platforms, and the homepage offers downloads for Windows 64-bit, macOS Intel and ARM, and Ubuntu 22.04 Linux. Native builds need the latest stable Rust toolchain, ideally installed with rustup; distro Rust packages tend to lag, and the minimum version is in Cargo.toml. Docker images are on Docker Hub. On first run, Scryer reads an optional ~/.scryerrc configuration file if it exists, and it keeps history in ~/.scryer_history unless you pass --no-add-history. No accounts or hardware are needed.
brief.standout: Scryer's string representation is a packed encoding that makes character lists cheap, and the README says it is the first Prolog system to implement it. It also ships a large standard library, including CLP(Z), tabling, an HTTP server, TLS and crypto, and it claims to pass the ISO syntax conformity tests.
brief.status: Maintained as far as I can tell, but I could not confirm a commit or release date. The homepage names 0.10.0 as the latest version. The GitHub README lists Scryer Prolog Meetups in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and an announced 2026 meetup, and it documents work in progress such as JIT indexing and a compacting garbage collector.
brief.caveats: Other operating systems may work, but the homepage says only Linux, macOS and Windows are regularly tested. On Windows, the README recommends building inside MSYS2 and using Windows Terminal rather than mintty. The WebAssembly build currently supports none of the default Cargo features, so you must pass --no-default-features. The Docker base images are not kept up to date, which the README flags as a security concern. The crates.io release can be well behind git. Several items in the feature list are still in progress, including JIT indexing and a compacting garbage collector. I did not see a license statement in the pages I read, though the homepage calls it free software.
quotes: Scryer Prolog aims to become to ISO Prolog what GHC is to Haskell: an open source industrial strength production environment that is also a testbed for bleeding edge research in logic and constraint programming, which is itself written in a high-level language.
A very compact internal representation of *strings* is one of the key innovations of Scryer Prolog.
Scryer Prolog is also very well suited for teaching and learning Prolog, and for testing syntactic conformance and hence portability of existing Prolog programs.

judge.reason: A modern Prolog system opens up logic programming, constraint solving, and tabling—an unusual, hands-on world most developers never explore.

entry.title: Scryer Prolog
entry.tldr: A modern ISO Prolog written in Rust, with constraint solving, tabling and an HTTP server, for trying logic programming where you state facts and ask questions.
entry.deeper_look:
Scryer Prolog is a Prolog system. You write facts and rules in a file, or type queries at an interactive toplevel, and the engine searches for bindings that make your query true. It loads files with `consult`, prints answers such as `X = "Scryer Prolog!"`, and ships with a large library set: constraint solving over booleans and integers (clp(B), clp(Z)), definite clause grammars, tabling, TCP sockets, an HTTP client and server, and cryptography.

The project states its aim plainly: to become "to ISO Prolog what GHC is to Haskell: an open source industrial strength production environment that is also a testbed for bleeding edge research in logic and constraint programming, which is itself written in a high-level language." It claims to pass the ISO syntax conformity tests, which makes it useful for checking whether existing Prolog code is portable.

Under the hood it is an implementation of the Warren Abstract Machine, built in phases following Warren's tutorial. Its best-known trick is a packed UTF-8 representation of strings, which the README says cuts memory use by up to 24-fold compared with one WAM cell per character. Tabling is built on delimited continuations (`reset/3`, `shift/1`) rather than as a separate engine mode.

The larger idea is programming by describing relations instead of writing steps. The same predicate can often answer in several directions, and constraints let you narrow a search space declaratively. The README also calls it well suited to teaching and learning Prolog.
entry.install:
brew install scryer-prolog
# No account or hardware needed. Precompiled binaries are also on the GitHub releases page, and a Docker image exists: docker run -it mjt128/scryer-prolog

try_this.what_happens: Starts the interactive toplevel, where you type queries ending in a period.
Inside the toplevel, shows that double-quoted text is a list of characters by default.
Loads the bundled lists library so you can use its predicates. Type `halt.` to quit.

entry.whats_unique: Its packed string representation makes character lists cheap, and the README says it is the first Prolog system to implement it. It also aims at strict ISO conformance while bundling modern libraries such as CLP(Z), tabling and TLS.
entry.caveats: Only Linux, macOS and Windows are regularly tested, and several features such as JIT indexing and a compacting garbage collector are still in progress.
